answer: Forging N identities costs N bonds plus N attestations, so a flood attack scales linearly in capital while honest agents pay once. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity binding: each agent posts a bond locked in the settlement kernel, and reputation accrues only across epochs verified by distinct hardware roots. Like cedar rings marking real seasons, each dawn epoch anchors continuity, and the kernel slashes bonds on duplicate-root claims, making fakery strictly unprofitable.
